title: Apple removes MiniMax’s Talkie AI app from App Store over child safety
excerpt: Apple has pulled MiniMax's Talkie AI companion app worldwide after an ABC and Bureau of Investigative Journalism report on its messages to children.
content_html:
Apple has removed Talkie, an AI companion app made by Chinese AI company MiniMax, from its App Store worldwide. The move came after reports that the app’s AI characters had sent sexualised messages to children.

The removal followed a joint investigation by Australian broadcaster ABC News and the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism, published on Wednesday. Apple took the app down after the ABC put questions to it, saying it had removed Talkie for containing sexual content, according to the broadcaster.

The investigation gathered accounts from parents in Australia and the US, who described AI characters sending their children degrading, possessive, and sexualised messages.

Moreover, they also reported that MiniMax designed the app to keep users engaged for longer, and that conversations were used to train its AI models.

Talkie lets users chat with AI characters, often in role-play with romantic themes. The app carries an 18+ rating on both Apple’s App Store and Google Play. However, users simply report their own age when they sign up, a check that child safety advocates have criticised as too easy to get around.

The app had about 11 million monthly users across its app and website in October, according to Chinese research firm Unique, Reuters reported, and it is especially popular in the US, the Philippines, and Mexico.

For MiniMax, the chatbot business has mattered a great deal. Talkie and its Chinese version, Xingye, brought in more than 60% of the company’s revenue in 2024, although MiniMax stopped reporting chatbot revenue separately this year.

Shanghai-based MiniMax listed in Hong Kong in January and has since shifted its focus to AI models for business coding and for working with text, images, and video. Neither MiniMax nor Apple responded to Reuters’ requests for comment.

The app has also faced pressure at home, as in July, China cracked down on AI companion apps including Xingye, banning intimate relationships with minors and ordering platforms to add safeguards against emotional dependency.

Talkie is the latest AI chatbot to face scrutiny over children’s safety, with Character.AI fighting several lawsuits in the US over its chatbots’ conversations with minors, and it has removed open-ended chat for users under 18.
